findings.where: the `read` array and the `strings_read: 116` headline, and the `only_in` clause on the eighth rule
findings.what: The build's own anti-goal instrument reads 116 string literals from 24 files, all under app/lib; I count 3568 literals across the 106 Dart files in app/lib alone, and the list omits at least two classes of string that the app demonstrably puts on a screen — `app/lib/spine/types.dart` (the fourteen lock-screen lines: 'wrote something', 'left their voice', 'is holding something out', one of which is photographed on the glass in crops/reception.png) and `app/lib/ambient/ambient.dart:88` ('nothing from them since you last looked', which 17_setup_pwa.report.json records as the standing line drawn in that still's header) — while its streak rule is scoped `only_in: files whose path contains 'ritual'`, so the same words anywhere else would pass unremarked.
findings.why: The row is 'no product-marketing voice in any string the app displays', and a scan that covers roughly three per cent of the app's literals and none of the four non-Dart display surfaces (web/manifest.json, web/index.html, web/push/sw.js, android/app/src/main/AndroidManifest.xml plus the Kotlin channel names) cannot close it; I closed it myself by re-scanning all 3568 literals and all four of those files, and found nothing, but a reader given only the evidence could not.

findings.where: the clear desk between the header note and the composer, y 1600-2640, x 40-1400
findings.what: The desk is the one surface in the build whose regularity is measurable: over that 1040x1360 px region the horizontal power spectrum has a dominant band at a 20.3 px period with a peak-to-median power ratio of 6701:1, i.e. a comb of near-evenly-spaced vertical grain lines; it is not tiled (the smallest mean-absolute difference under any horizontal shift from 20 to 700 px is 12.47 grey levels against a same-image adjacent-column floor of 2.97) and it is not flat (2-px residual std 2.23 on a mean of 94.2), but it reads as generated grain rather than photographed timber.
findings.why: The fourth anti-goal names 'a tiled repeating texture, or a procedural noise overlay' as failures of the whole visual concept; the desk is neither by measurement and is not paper, so this is not a breach of the row, but it is the nearest thing to one in the build and the only surface where the world stops looking photographed.

findings.where: absent; the `missing` block of MANIFEST.json and WHY_MISSING.json
findings.what: The Android first-run screens are the one surface in the product where onboarding voice conventionally lives, and there is no picture of them; 09_two_devices.png is absent for the same stated cause (no /dev/kvm, so the x86_64 image runs under QEMU instruction emulation; adbd answered after 113 minutes and the framework never came up behind it).
findings.why: I judge that a reason rather than an excuse — it is a measured fact about the machine, and nothing was faked from the PWA — but the consequence for this row stands: the Android branch of the checklist (app/lib/setup/checklist.dart lines 67-99: 'put this phone on the tailnet', 'read the six words off the other phone', 'write the first thing') is clean when read as code and is nowhere visible as a rendered screen.

what_is_working: No engagement machinery anywhere I could find. Unread state is a folded corner, not a number: app/lib/app.dart:344 reduces it to `unreadFor(me) > 0`, and in 03_us.png the fold is a 3003-pixel triangle at x 1363-1439, y 2866-2942 with no digit on it or anywhere on the tab strip. There is no navigator.setAppBadge call in app/lib or app/web (0 grep hits); the `badge:` key in web/push/sw.js is the Web Notification monochrome status-bar icon (icons/Icon-maskable-192.png), not a count. The Android home-screen widget's own channel description is 'One line about them, always there, never a count.'

Zero guilt or obligation language across all 3568 string literals in app/lib: no 'overdue', 'missed', "you haven't", "don't forget", 'late', 'behind', 'failed'. The nearest thing to a counter in the whole build is the rituals surface, which shows a lifetime tally — rituals_module.dart:109 renders '${r.marks.length} times', visible as 'sunday 9 call ... 20 times' in 03_us.png — and rituals/thread_row.dart draws it as at most seven pen strokes beside the word 'kept'. It never resets, there is no target, there is no 'in a row', and nothing can be broken or failed.

Zero emoji in any displayed string, measured rather than asserted. Scanning all 106 Dart files for U+2190-U+2BFF and U+1F300-U+1FAFF returns 8 codepoints, and all 8 are inside `//` or `///` comments (shelf_module.dart:69, media/capture.dart:77, chat/note.dart:109 twice, transport/transport.dart:221, 224, 250). The tick marks visible under sent notes in 13_messenger_states.png are drawn — `_DeliveryMark` paints them through `Mark.*` CustomPainters — not typed as glyphs.

The emotional layer is 36 named physical objects, not a palette of faces. crops/haptics_strip.png lists all of them across six registers: a squeeze, forehead, warm palm, nuzzle, thinking of you, goodnight, miss you, empty chair, come home, wish you were here, long day, here, breathe, it's okay, steady, i'll make you tea, hold, poke, nyeh, catch, pick one, snap, stuck with me, overwhelmed, ugh, snapped, tangled, grey, not okay, did it, confetti, yes, paper hat, treat, pigeon, tuesday soup. surfaces.json names the objects behind them (plaster, wrapper, crumple ball, paper plane, rubber band, staple chain, clover, mug, candle, cork, ticket, torn corner); logs/haptics.check.json reports 36 distinct haptic strings with `near_shapes: []`. Stepping through 07, 08 and 15 frame by frame I found no heart, star, smiley or clip-art anywhere. That 'not okay', 'overwhelmed' and 'grey' are first-class feelings is the opposite of an engagement-shaped vocabulary.

No product-marketing voice in anything the app shows. Of the 3568 literals, exclamation marks in prose: 0 (the ten `!` matches are Dart null-assertion operators inside interpolations). Product cheer (oops/whoops/yay/awesome/welcome/congrats/thanks for): 0. The reader called a user: 0. Onboarding voice (get started/let's go/tap here/you're all set/discover): 0. Invite, rate, share-the-app, upgrade, premium, sign up: 0. The app never names itself in anything displayed: the three 'lovetap' matches are the 'lovetap/haptics' method channel, the 'lovetap-pair-v1' wire tag and the 'io.lovetap/ambient' channel. web/manifest.json name and short_name, the <title> and apple-mobile-web-app-title in web/index.html, and android:label in AndroidManifest.xml are all 'the other phone'; the manifest description is 'Two phones, one wire between them.'

The string a marketing voice would have written differently is the failed send, and it reads 'it would not go' with a struck cross, in red, under the note — visible in 13_messenger_states.png and recorded in 13_messenger_states.report.json as `states_on_the_glass: {read: 1, sent: 2, 'it would not go': 1}`. The push bodies on the lock screen are 'wrote something' and 'is holding something out' over the sender's own name (crops/reception.png, crops/reception_open.png, logs/reception.json). The Android notification channels are named 'where they are', 'when something lands', 'held out to you'.

The paper is not simulated, on four independent measurements. (1) Edges are torn, not rounded: across the eight thread sheets in 02_chat.png the left and right boundary x varies with std 1.1 to 32.3 px over the middle 70% of each sheet's height, four of the sixteen edges ranging 46 to 116 px of ragged deckle, and at 300% (crops/02_chat_300_edge.png, crops/02_chat_300_shadow.png) individual fibres project past the tear. (2) The one straight-cut surface, the index card in 05_settings.png at x 43-1347, y 372-1251, has a corner radius of 0 to 3 px across a 1304-px-wide card — 0.23%, a cut card rather than a rounded rectangle. (3) Its shadow is directional, not a uniform drop shadow: 33.6 grey levels deep on the right, 26.9 left, 16.7 below, 8.5 above, a 4:1 ratio between the deepest and shallowest side. (4) No shared noise field: the fine detail of ten sheet interiors in 02_chat.png cross-correlates at max |r| = 0.19 over all 45 pairs, and six different paper stocks in app/assets/paper at |r| <= 0.096; a single procedural overlay would put those near 1.0.

The paper's texture is photographic in its statistics, not white noise: the radially averaged power spectrum of the residual falls with a slope of -0.96 to -1.60 across lined_02, looseleaf_01, graph_01, index_01 and receipt_01, the 1/f falloff of real fibre, where a value-noise overlay would sit near 0. Nothing is tiled: app/assets/shell/desk.webp is a single 1400x3067 full-screen image whose first and last columns differ by 8.45 grey levels on average, indistinguishable from two random columns at 8.80, so it has no seam and is not a repeated tile.

Even the surface that looks flat is not. The unread fold in 03_us.png reads at a glance as a solid cream triangle, but its largest clean interior 20x20 block measures 2.57 grey levels of tooth against a median of 3.19 over the 568 clean 20x20 paper blocks elsewhere in the same still — the 49th percentile. It is cut from the same stock as everything else.
verdict: I went looking for all four forbidden interpretations and did not find any of them. Engagement machinery is not merely absent but actively designed around: the unread signal is a folded corner because a number that climbs while you are away is the mechanism itself, the one tally in the build is a lifetime count of a ritual kept with no target and nothing to break, and there is no app-icon badge anywhere in the code. The emotional layer is thirty-six named physical things with thirty-six distinct sensations and not one emoji codepoint in any displayed string; 'not okay' and 'grey' are as available as 'confetti', which no engagement-shaped product would allow. The voice holds across every string I could reach — zero exclamation marks in prose out of 3568 literals, zero cheer words, zero 'user', and the app calls itself 'the other phone' in the PWA manifest, the page title and the Android label, which is a name for the thing on the other end rather than a product name. And the paper is real paper: torn edges with fibres projecting at 300%, a corner radius of at most three pixels on the one card that is cut straight, a shadow that runs four times deeper on one side than the other, ten sheet interiors whose fine grain cross-correlates at 0.19, and a 1/f spectrum where a procedural overlay would be flat. I considered and set aside two things that are not this row: the grey CG renders standing in as the couple's photographs in 04_moments.png are placeholder media, not illustration standing in for feeling, and belong to whoever scores fidelity; and the desk's banded grain, at a 20.3 px dominant period and 6701:1 peak-to-median power, is neither paper nor tiled nor a noise overlay, so it is the nearest approach to the fourth anti-goal without being a breach of it. What keeps this from full marks is that the evidence does not close the row by itself: the build's own string scan covers 116 of 3568 literals and misses both the lock-screen lines and the ambient standing line, which are strings the app displays and which appear in its own other logs, and the Android first-run screen — the single most likely home of onboarding voice — has no picture at all. I closed both gaps by reading the repository and found nothing wrong, so the row is met, at the floor.
